This neuron's activations are all negative: it is maximally suppressed on the `<|begin_of_text|>` token (and moderately on ordinary words), and comes closest to zero on sentence-terminating periods (including "." followed by a newline) — so functionally it marks end-of-sentence punctuation versus document-start/regular tokens.

L5·N696unmasked layer
Fires at sentence-boundary tokens where the closing period is fused with the following newline or capitalized word (".\n", ".F", ".If"), i.e. the end-of-sentence position (also the attribution "said" ending a quote); the same surface forms can also drive it strongly negative, so it's a sentence-break detector rather than a semantic one.
